summary: French uses être broadly for copular and locative predication, while il y a is the central presentational/existential construction.

semantic_map.SEM.CURRENT_STATE: être + state adjective/PP; lexical predicates may use other verbs
semantic_map.SEM.RESULTANT_STATE: être + adjective/participle where a state reading is intended; distinguish passive
semantic_map.SEM.ENTITY_LOCATION: être + locative expression / se trouver as lexical location alternative
semantic_map.SEM.EVENT_LOCATION: être / avoir lieu + locative expression depending event construction
semantic_map.SEM.ABSENCE_NONEXISTENCE: il n’y a pas de + NP
semantic_map.SEM.ORIGIN_AFFILIATION: être de / venir de / nationality predicate depending meaning
semantic_map.SEM.MATERIAL_COMPOSITION: être en/de + material; être fait de for composition
semantic_map.SEM.POSSESSION_AS_EXISTENCE: not default; dedicated avoir is ordinary possession
